# SellWant

> A free two-sided marketplace for event tickets — student parties, formals,
> concerts. People post tickets they are **selling** and tickets they are
> **looking for**. Offers are public, so the going rate is visible before
> anyone commits. There are no fees, no commission, and no booking charge:
> SellWant never touches the money and never holds the ticket.

## What makes it different

**It is free.** No listing fee, no seller fee, no buyer fee, no service
charge, no payment processing cut. The two people agree a price and pay each
other directly, usually Venmo or Zelle. SellWant is not a payment processor
and takes nothing.

**Both sides are public.** Most ticket sites show only what sellers are
asking. Here you can also see what buyers are offering, and every offer and
counter-offer on a listing is visible. That is the point: it turns a private
haggle in a group chat into a visible market price.

**No `.edu` requirement.** Anyone can post or buy.

## The model

Two listing types, and the distinction matters when reading a page:

- **sell** — someone has a ticket and names a price. Marked up as
  `schema.org/Offer`.
- **want** — someone needs a ticket and names what they will pay. Marked up as
  `schema.org/Demand`. This is not a product page that is out of stock; it is
  a standing request, and answering it means offering to sell.

The headline figure on a listing is the **going rate**: the highest offer on a
sell listing, the lowest on a want listing. A counter-offer from the person
who posted the listing is shown but excluded from that figure — it is their
own asking price, not evidence of demand.

**Money never moves through SellWant.** "Buying" means agreeing a price and a
place to meet. The platform cannot see, verify, hold, or refund a payment, and
there is nothing to charge a fee on.

**The handoff is physical.** Tickets are usually static QR codes that cannot
be transferred, so the seller keeps a working copy. The two people meet and
scan in together. There is no digital delivery.

## For agents

Reading is open and unauthenticated:

- [All active listings as JSON](https://sellwant.com/api/listings.json) — id,
  url, type, price, going rate, offer count, date, location
- [Sitemap](https://sellwant.com/sitemap.xml) — every active listing URL
- [Feed](https://sellwant.com/) — the same market as HTML
- Listing pages carry JSON-LD: `Event` with either `Offer` or `Demand`

An agent can usefully **find, compare and negotiate**: search listings, read
the going rate, draft an offer for its person to approve.

An agent **cannot complete a trade**. Someone has to turn up at a door. Any
flow ending in "purchased" is wrong; the honest end state is "a price is
agreed and a meeting is arranged".

### What does not exist yet

Being explicit so nothing is attempted that cannot work:

- **There is no write API.** Posting a listing, making an offer, accepting one
  — all require a signed-in person using the site.
- **There is no MCP server yet.** One is intended, so that an agent can search
  and draft offers on its person's behalf. Anything committing money will need
  that person's explicit approval, because the counterparty is a stranger and
  the payment is irreversible.

Only **active** listings are exposed anywhere. Sold and cancelled ones are
withheld deliberately: a completed trade's price belongs to the two people who
made it.

## Optional

- [Sign in](https://sellwant.com/signin) — needed to post or offer, never to browse
- Identity (names, Instagram handles, completed-handoff counts) is visible
  only to signed-in people. Contact details are visible only to the two
  parties in an agreed deal. Nothing in the public data exposes either.
